summary: William Henry Denham Rouse was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Cheltenham College, Regent's Park College, and the University of Cambridge. He held posts at Bedford School, Cheltenham College, Rugby School, and was headmaster at The Perse School (1902–1928).

William Herschel held posts with the Hanoverian Foot Guards (~1753–1758), County Durham Militia and Volunteers, Charles Avison, and at Leeds. He later served at the Octagon Chapel, Bath (1767–1780), Bath Philharmonia (1780–1782), and Observatory House (1782–1822).

William Hodge Mill worked in Indology and religious studies. After studying at Trinity College, Cambridge (~1809–1813), he served as Principal of Bishop's College, Kolkata (~1820–1838), and held a post at the University of Cambridge (~1848–1853).
William Homan Thorpe studied at Jesus College, Cambridge (~1921–1924). He later served at the University of Cambridge from approximately 1932 to 1969, where he taught John Hurrell Crook.

William James was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Plymouth College and Harvard University, including Harvard Medical School. He held successive positions teaching physiology and philosophy at Harvard University from 1872 until becoming professor in 1885.

William Jones, a scholar of Indology and linguistics, studied at Harrow, University College, Oxford, and Middle Temple, learning under teachers including Ramchandra and Ramalocana. He served as Chief Justice at Fort William in 1783 and founded The Asiatic Society in 1784.

William L. Ames works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He earned his M.S. at Caltech and Ph.D. at the University of Washington under Collett Cox and David Seyfort Ruegg, later holding posts at John F. Kennedy University and other institutions.

William M. Bodiford specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at the University of Kansas, Tsukuba, Komazawa, and Yale under Stanley Weinstein. He taught at Davidson College and the University of Iowa before joining UCLA as professor of Asian languages and cultures.

William M. Gorvine is a scholar in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned his B.A. from Connecticut College and his M.A. and Ph.D. from the University of Virginia, studying under David Germano, Jeffrey Hopkins, and William Magee, among others.

William Magee specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins. He held posts at the University of Virginia, the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies, and Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts.

William Marshall Smart studied at the University of Glasgow (~1906–1910) and Trinity College, Cambridge (~1910–1914). He subsequently held posts at the University of Cambridge (~1919–1937) and the University of Glasgow (~1937–1959).

William Muir was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Kilmarnock Academy, the University of Edinburgh (~1834–1836), and Haileybury (~1836–1837), later serving as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Edinburgh (~1885–1903).
William P. Chu is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of California, Los Angeles, earning his MA by 2006 under the supervision of Robert E. Buswell Jr.

William Price was a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He taught oriental languages at Netherstone House Seminary and served as Professor of Hindústaní at Fort William College (~1813–1830).

William R. Hutchison worked in religious studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Oxford (~1951–1953) and Yale (~1953–1956). After posts at Yale, Hunter College, American University, and Wisconsin-Madison, he held positions at Harvard University and Harvard Divinity School (~1968–2005).

William R. LaFleur studied at Calvin University, the University of Michigan, and the University of Chicago. A scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, he held faculty posts at Princeton (~1971–1978), UCLA (~1978–1989), and the University of Pennsylvania (~1990–2010).

William Rainey Harper studied at Muskingum and Yale under William Dwight Whitney. Specializing in linguistics and religious studies, he taught at Muskingum, Denison, Baptist Union Seminary, and Yale, before serving as president of the University of Chicago (1891–1906) and Bradley University (~1897–1906).

William Robertson was a historian who studied divinity at the University of Edinburgh (1733–1741). He served as Principal of the University of Edinburgh starting in 1762 and was a member of the Royal Society of Edinburgh and the Russian Academy of Sciences.

William Roxburgh studied at the University of Edinburgh and Marischal College. He held positions with the Madras Medical Service, managed the Samalkot Experimental Farm, and served as superintendent of the Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden and Keeper of Edinburgh's Royal Botanic Garden.

William Shi-Yuan Wang, a scholar in linguistics and sinology, studied at Columbia and the University of Michigan. He held posts at MIT, Ohio State, UC Berkeley (1966–1994), City University of Hong Kong, CUHK, National Taiwan Normal University, and Hong Kong Polytechnic University.
